items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: What did you think of the — I guess they would have called it the avante garde period, free jazz and so forth, that Ornette was doing...

ctx.x: Oh yeah. That orchestra I think Jimmy Owens had a great deal to do with that orchestra. And I got to write quite a few things for them. It was a wonderful experience because I was free to do whatever I wanted to, usually some kind of direction in the program, but it was a chance to have the freedom as far as the things that I wanted to try, the things that I wanted to experiment with and all of that. It was a wonderful opportunity for me so I think I had a chance to do a lot of good things there, to learn a lot…
What did you think of the — I guess they would have called it the avante garde period, free jazz and so forth, that Ornette was doing and some of Coltrane’s later work.

We did a lot of that in Europe already before I came back you know. In fact in Europe they had some subsidy for projects that were based on free music, that means that you were usually doing things that were somewhat unusual to the way that you usually approach composing or writing music. And I thought it was a thing that had a good effect on, in general, on our musical growth, because it was a chance for us to experience something different in music. And it was a chance to do something that ordinarily would —…
